h.strategy: Use the retrieved work from other fields as a source of mechanisms that transfer to this system: redundancy and robustness in networks, complementarity versus substitution of inputs, bottlenecks and rate limits in flows, diminishing returns, and interference between processes. For each hypothesis, state which borrowed mechanism it instantiates, and use every mechanism at most twice. Do not condition on the current value of the edited field itself, and do not use conditions that simply make the edited part unused or disconnected; experts see both as obvious. Prefer interactions between two different fields where the predicted direction contradicts the naive expectation. Spread hypotheses across many edit fields and condition fields and both directions. In each 'why', give the mechanism and the specific comparison that would refute it.

hyps.why: Two cascaded pools over-smooth, so the e2 pool costs more after a pooled e0.
With e1 already supplying conv3x3 features to node 2, a 1x1 on e5 adds a smaller marginal gain.
An identity sibling into node 2 interferes with or duplicates the conv output from e1, shrinking its gain.
A bypass is most valuable when the deep path through e2 is the fragile one.
Pooling features just produced by a conv3x3 discards the detail the conv created.
With a conv input from e1 already feeding node 2, a parallel identity route from node 1 is redundant.
A strong downstream e5 can only exploit what node 2 receives from e1, so improving e1 is amplified.
Early pooling denoises the input consumed by a downstream conv3x3 on e4, so it costs less.
An unsmoothed identity from e5 complements a pooled sibling at node 3.
With an identity sibling into node 2, a high-gain conv on e2 sums at a mismatched scale and gains less.
